stemMd: A block slides horizontally at constant velocity while a 14 N horizontal pull acts on it. What is the magnitude of the opposing friction force, assuming no other horizontal forces?

options.label: D
options.textMd: It depends only on the block's speed.

explanationMd: Constant velocity means zero acceleration and hence zero net horizontal force. Friction must exactly balance the 14 N pull, so its magnitude is 14 N.

distractorRationale.b: No condition halves the pulling force.
distractorRationale.e: Constant velocity implies zero net force, not zero friction.
distractorRationale.c: Doubling friction would produce a net backward force.
distractorRationale.d: The force balance already determines friction here.
